tagline: The 'pearl of the Mediterranean' on Morocco's Rif coast — Al Hoceima's port and the Quemado and Cala Bonita beaches beneath a national park, a wild bay linked today only by mountain road.
summary: Al Hoceima is a Mediterranean resort town on Morocco's Rif coast, set on a dramatic bay of cliffs and coves — Quemado Beach in town, Cala Bonita and Sfiha nearby, and the offshore islet of Peñón de Alhucemas — fringed by the Al Hoceima National Park. Its port serves fishing and small-craft traffic, and the coast west toward Cala Iris and east along the park is spectacular but reachable today only by slow, winding mountain roads. Demand is tourism- and leisure-led and seasonal, concentrated in the summer and drawing on the Rif's diaspora traffic and Morocco's record national tourism year. A clean foiling-electric layer fits the short protected bay hops (Pioneer II) and the longer coastal legs to the national-park coves (Quanta-LR at range edge), opening a wild, hard-to-reach coast to fast, quiet sea access. Note: no boarding points are sealed here yet — Al Hoceima is a priority mint candidate.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The short protected bay hops — port ↔ Cala Bonita / Quemado (~1–2 nm) — sit comfortably inside the ~70 nm all-electric envelope, with shore charging at the town port.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The longer, exposed Rif-coast leg to Cala Iris (~20 nm) at range edge uses the Quanta-LR roadmap tier for stability on an open Mediterranean coast.

competitive_landscape: Today: winding Rif mountain roads, the fishing port, and diesel day-boats; no clean fast-passenger coastal service.
seasonality: Strongly summer-peaked leisure demand; calmer Mediterranean summer conditions suit high-frequency foiling rotations, with wind exposure on the open national-park legs.
regulatory_note: Port of Al Hoceima under ANP; the national-park coast carries protected-area constraints that suit low-wake, zero-emission craft.
